4. `reversalWireDigest` uses `encodeFrozenWireDigest({ ...invoice, status: "VOIDED" })`.

Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. - IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. - Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. tools.name: Edit
tools.description:

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. content.text:
## Plan for T06: SettlementRegistry and void reversal

### Findings
- `applyCredits` in `src/creditPool.mjs` ignores `asOfMs`. It doesn't filter by `effectiveFromMs` or `expiresAtMs`, it doesn't sort, and it mutates the grants it is given. Existing tests rely on it, so I won't change it. The registry will pass it a pre-filtered, pre-sorted list of the registry's own grants.
- `summarizePoolBalance` also ignores `asOfMs` and counts every grant with `remainingCents > 0`. `getRegistrySnapshot` therefore has to filter active grants itself. I'll either extend it with a backward-compatible filter or compute the balance in the registry.
- `buildInvoice` calls `applyCredits` on whatever grants it gets. It doesn't filter or sort, so `settleInvoice` must pass in the active, sorted grants.
- `INVOICE_STATUS.VOIDED` already exists in `src/constants.mjs`, so that file stays untouched. `encodeFrozenWireDigest` reads `invoiceId`, `accountId`, `currency`, `totalDueCents` and `status`, so `{...invoice, status:'VOIDED'}` works as specified.

### Changes

**1. `src/errors.mjs`**
- Append `ERR_UNKNOWN_INVOICE` and `ERR_ALREADY_VOIDED` to `ERROR_CODES`, with each value equal to its key. Leave the existing codes as they are.

**2. `src/creditPool.mjs`** (helpers only; leave `applyCredits` and `summarizePoolBalance` as they are)
- `selectActiveGrantsOrdered(grants, asOfMs)` filters grants where `remainingCents > 0 && effectiveFromMs <= asOfMs && asOfMs < expiresAtMs`. It sorts by `expiresAtMs` ascending, then `grantId` ascending, using a plain `<`/`>` comparison rather than `localeCompare`. It returns the same grant object references so debits land in registry state.
- `restoreAllocations(grants, allocations, voidedAtMs)` finds each grant by `grantId` and adds `appliedCents` back to `remainingCents`. It returns `{ restoredActiveCents, restoredExpiredCents }`, splitting on `voidedAtMs < grant.expiresAtMs` versus `>=`.
- Optional: export a pool-balance helper that sums only grants active at `asOfMs`.

**3. `src/invoiceBuilder.mjs`**
- `createSettlementRegistry(initialGrants = [])`:
  - Validate that the input is an array, otherwise throw `ERR_INVALID_CONFIG`.
  - Return `{ grants: initialGrants.map(g => ({...g})), invoices: new Map() }`. Cloning means the caller's objects are never mutated.
- `settleInvoice(registry, params)`:
  - Call `buildInvoice({...params, grants: selectActiveGrantsOrdered(registry.grants, params.asOfMs ?? 0)})`. The grants are the registry's own objects, so `applyCredits` debits registry state directly.
  - Store the finalized invoice in the registry and return it.
  - Decide what to do about a duplicate `invoiceId`. I'd throw `ERR_INVALID_CONFIG` before any debit. This isn't in the spec, so it's an open choice.
  - Store the allocations as a copy so later mutation can't change them.
- `voidInvoiceSettlement(registry, invoiceId, voidedAtMs)`:
  - Throw `LedgerError(ERR_UNKNOWN_INVOICE)` if the invoice is missing.
  - Throw `ERR_ALREADY_VOIDED` if its status is already `VOIDED`.
  - Otherwise call `restoreAllocations`, set `invoice.status = 'VOIDED'`, and compute `reversalWireDigest = encodeFrozenWireDigest({...invoice, status:'VOIDED'})`.
  - Compute `netDeltaCents = invoice.totalDueCents === 0 ? 0 : -invoice.totalDueCents`, which avoids `-0`.
  - Return `{ invoiceId, status:'VOIDED', voidedAtMs, netDeltaCents, restoredActiveCents, restoredExpiredCents, reversalWireDigest }`.
- `getRegistrySnapshot(registry, asOfMs = 0)`:
  - Return `{ invoices: [...] (insertion order, cloned), grants: [...] (cloned), poolBalance }`.
  - `poolBalance` comes from the active grants at `asOfMs`, so restored expired credits are excluded.

### Edge cases covered
- **Restored expired grants:** their `remainingCents` increases, but they stay excluded from later settles because the active filter requires `asOfMs < expiresAtMs`.
- **Zero-total invoices:** `netDeltaCents` is `0`, never `-0`.
- **Voiding twice:** the second call throws `ERR_ALREADY_VOIDED`, and the failed call changes no state.
- **Unknown invoice:** throws `ERR_UNKNOWN_INVOICE`.
- **Insufficient credit:** an invoice with leftover `totalDueCents` gets `netDeltaCents = -totalDueCents`.
- **Multiple allocations:** a void can restore across several grants, some active and some expired.
- **Grant no longer in the registry:** skip it safely.
- **Isolation:** snapshots return clones, so callers can't mutate registry state.
- **Boundary:** `voidedAtMs === expiresAtMs` counts as expired.

### Verification
- Run `node --test test/` and check that all existing tests still pass along with `task_visible.test.mjs`.
- Add a few ad hoc checks for these cases:
  - Void after expiry, then settle again to confirm the restored credits are not used.
  - A double void.
  - An unknown invoice.
  - An invoice with a nonzero total due.
  - The `-0` normalization.
  - That the input grants aren't mutated.
  - Two grants with the same expiry, where `grantId` breaks the tie.

I added the settlement registry and invoice void reversal, and `npm test` passes: 10 of 10, including the T06 visible test and all the existing ones. I only ran the supplied tests. I didn't run my own checks for the edge cases from the plan, such as voiding after expiry, a double void, or the `-0` result.

- **`src/errors.mjs`**: I added `ERR_UNKNOWN_INVOICE` and `ERR_ALREADY_VOIDED` and left the existing codes unchanged.
- **`src/creditPool.mjs`**: I added two helpers and left `applyCredits` and `summarizePoolBalance` as they were.
  - `selectActiveGrantsOrdered` returns the grants usable at `asOfMs`, ordered by `expiresAtMs` then `grantId`.
  - `restoreAllocations` adds the cents back to each grant and splits them into active and expired by `voidedAtMs`.
- **`src/invoiceBuilder.mjs`**: I added the four registry functions. The registry clones the input grants, so the caller's objects are never mutated. `voidInvoiceSettlement` returns the shape the spec asks for, with `netDeltaCents` normalized so it is never `-0`.
  - **Expired grants:** a restored credit on an expired grant is added back to that grant but is never usable by a later `settleInvoice`.
  - **Snapshots:** `settleInvoice` and `getRegistrySnapshot` return copies, so callers can't change the registry's stored state.

The spec doesn't cover settling the same `invoiceId` twice. I made that throw `ERR_INVALID_CONFIG` before any credit is debited. Say so if you'd rather it behave differently.

I didn't touch `src/frozenWire.mjs` or `src/constants.mjs`.
